findings.detail: The warning joins `sites.unparsed` in full: on the Night Back fixture that is one line, but the count is bounded only by how many priced-looking lines a site has across up to 13 pages. A site with 40 such lines (menus with ranges, combo offers, bare trailing numbers — exactly what `classifyLine` routes to `unparsed`) produces a single multi-kilobyte log entry that pushes every other warning out of view, including the `other language` and `could not be read` notices logged immediately before it. The data is already exported losslessly on the `Google Sites pages` sheet by `googleSitesReportSheet`, so the log does not need to carry all of it.
findings.summary: Unparsed-line warning interpolates every unparsed line into one log entry

findings.detail: `fetchGoogleSitesMenu` runs from line 161 to 290 — about 125 lines in one function, past the 80-line threshold in handbooks/general/code-smells.md, with four numbered phases (read first page, collect+read linked pages, partition by script, OCR fallback) and nesting that reaches four levels inside the image loop (if → for → try → catch). It is new code in this diff, not a legacy function being touched, and the numbered comments are effectively section headers marking where the seams already are. The cost is concrete: the OCR block (235-278) cannot be unit-tested without first driving the whole page-reading pipeline into a zero-rows state, which is why every image test has to stub six page fetches to 503 (tests/unit/googleSites.test.ts `hubOnly()`).
findings.summary: fetchGoogleSitesMenu is ~125 lines across four phases
